title: No Hands Slab
texts: Hands-free slab climbing to practice foot engagement

The goal of this workout is to learn how to engage your feet to initiate climbing movements instead of pulling with your arms.  

Find an inclined (slab) wall with large holds. Using only your feet, climb the entire wall without using your hands for assistance.  Your hands can float above holds to catch you if you feel you would slip, but refrain from using them to initiate movements.  The chosen climb should be easy enough that you can complete a significant portion of the climb without the use of your hands.  This can be completed using a set problem or by adding other holds to the climb.  

Once you have completed the climb, rest for 1-2 minutes before repeating the problem again, for a total of 6 repititions.  As you improve, you can make the climb more challenging by removing holds or using smaller foot holds.
